key_insight: Deep sequence models are more robust than tabular baselines for PV power forecasting when NWP inputs are noisy, because they better filter correlated forecast errors and adapt their reliance toward stable signals.
engineering_relevance: For PV plant operations, model choice should consider not only nominal accuracy but also robustness and latency under realistic forecast uncertainty, especially when NWP errors are state dependent and physically coupled.
method: Simulated a controlled PV forecasting testbed using virtual PV power to isolate input-uncertainty propagation.
Injected dynamic NWP perturbations with clear-sky-modulated heteroscedasticity and radiation-consistent Erbs reconstruction.
Compared six models, including PatchTST, GRU, N-HITS, and LightGBM, then used SHAP and Integrated Gradients to interpret feature reallocation under corruption.
evidence_signal: The evaluation used dynamic perturbation scenarios rather than perfect-forecast assumptions, enabling robustness testing across medium to high disturbance regimes and comparison with clean-condition accuracy and latency.
watch_item: The robustness conclusions are based on a simulated virtual-PV framework, so real-world performance may vary with site-specific sensor errors, weather regimes, and deployment constraints.
paper_title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
